title: Quantinuum and HQS Simulate 21-Spin NMR Spectrum on 42 Qubits With 1,400+ Two-Qubit Gate Circuits - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantinuum and HQS Quantum Simulations ran an end-to-end digital NMR simulation of a 22-spin diphosphane molecule on the H2-1 trapped-ion machine using 42 qubits and up to 1,442 two-qubit gates, resolving a double-peak structure at about 0.07 ppm. The authors concede classical solvers like Spinach remain more efficient for routine cases.

insights.claim: The benchmark modeled the proton NMR spectrum of 1,2-di-tert-butyl-diphosphane, a 22-spin molecule with two 31P and twenty 1H nuclei, on Quantinuum's H2-1 trapped-ion computer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Largest-scale digital NMR simulation cited here on trapped-ion hardware.

insights.claim: Projecting the two-phosphorus subsystem into its singlet-triplet subspace cut the system from 22 spins to a 21-spin effective Hamiltonian, reducing two-qubit gates per Trotter step from 69 to 20 native ZZPhase gates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Problem-specific compression is key to fitting near-term hardware.
insights.locator: To map the molecular spin network

insights.claim: The run used 42 qubits (21 system plus 21 ancilla for leakage detection), 70 Trotter steps of 0.42 ms covering 29.4 ms, and a maximum two-qubit gate depth of 1,442.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives a depth and qubit-count benchmark for H2-1.
insights.locator: Quantinuum H2-1 NMR Simulation Technical Parameters

insights.claim: The run reproduced the double-peak structure in the 3.9-4.3 ppm region at roughly 0.07 ppm resolution, which earlier 22-qubit superconducting and trapped-ion experiments had struggled to resolve, helped by all-to-all connectivity and idle-error mitigation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Supports trapped-ion connectivity advantage for deep simulations.

insights.claim: The error suppression stack combined echo compiling, full-Trotter-step Pauli twirling, server-side dynamical decoupling and ancilla-assisted leakage post-selection.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Illustrates software-level error mitigation as a performance lever.
insights.locator: Quantinuum H2-1 NMR Simulation Technical Parameters

insights.claim: The authors note classical solvers like Spinach remain more computationally efficient for routine high-field liquid-state spectroscopy today, so the result validates workflow viability rather than showing advantage.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: No quantum advantage claim here; value is a stepping stone.

insights.claim: The result is said to validate deep digital Hamiltonian simulation workflows for zero- to ultralow-field NMR and solid-state materials characterization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: ZULF NMR and materials are plausible niches where classical methods struggle.
